title: H2@Work Employee Spotlight: Dylan Stratton
summary: At Plug’s Rochester Innovation Center, Dylan Stratton oversees the first shift teams responsible for Electrolyzer (ELX) stack assembly, testing, and validation.
body_markdown:
At Plug’s Rochester Innovation Center, Dylan Stratton oversees the first shift teams responsible for Electrolyzer (ELX) stack assembly, testing, and validation. His role brings together people, equipment, and processes to help build and validate Plug’s electrolyzer technology. Having been part of the Rochester operation since its early days, Dylan has seen the facility grow and has played a role in bringing new products and processes to life.


## Finding a New Opportunity at Plug


Dylan’s journey to Plug began when he was working remotely for another company and felt ready for a change. His father mentioned an opportunity at Plug, and Dylan decided to apply. The Rochester business was growing rapidly, and the opportunity offered something different from his previous roles.


Although the work was in a new field, he was excited to learn something new and take on the challenge. What started as an opportunity to try something different soon became a chance to be involved in building a product from the ground up.


## Bringing a Product to Life


One of the things Dylan enjoys most about working at Plug is seeing how different parts of the business come together. From reviewing engineering prints and setting up production equipment to developing work instructions and refining manufacturing processes, he has been involved in several stages of bringing electrolyzer technology into production.


He describes it as a rewarding experience to be part of a team tasked with developing a cutting-edge product and finding ways to manufacture it at a scale that had never been achieved before.


## Growing Alongside Rochester


For Dylan, one of the most memorable experiences has been being part of Plug Rochester from the beginning. Since joining in 2021, he has watched the building take shape, experienced the trial and error involved in the early days of stack assembly, and seen manufacturing processes evolve over time.


Along the way, he has also had the opportunity to work with talented colleagues and learn from people across different teams. Those experiences have made the journey especially meaningful.


## The Importance of People and Communication


Building something new comes with its share of challenges. Dylan says one of the biggest has been getting all the essential pieces in place, including the right people, parts, and processes.


With so many teams involved, coordination can sometimes be challenging. His approach is to get to know as many people as possible and build good working relationships. He believes that being kind and communicating openly can make a significant difference, especially when you need support from someone down the road.


## Taking Small Steps Toward a Cleaner Future


What excites Dylan about hydrogen is its potential to provide a cleaner form of energy with fewer environmental consequences than many traditional energy sources.


He recognizes that the infrastructure needed for widespread hydrogen fuel cell adoption is still developing. However, he finds it exciting to contribute to the progress being made today, knowing that every step helps move the industry forward.


## Keep Learning and Keep Things Light


Dylan’s philosophy is simple: do not take everything too seriously. He believes in keeping things light and fun while making sure the important work gets done.


He also believes in staying open to new experiences. Whether it is learning a new skill or trying something for the first time, he encourages taking opportunities to step outside your comfort zone.


## Life Outside Plug


Outside of work, Dylan enjoys spending time outdoors. Hunting, fishing, golfing, riding dirt bikes, and skiing are among his favorite activities. He also grew up playing hockey and lacrosse and enjoys traveling to new places and spending time with friends.


One special member of his family is Remy, his beautiful one-and-a-half-year-old Golden Retriever, who keeps life interesting outside the workplace.
